title: Set a luggage pull handle to its marked working length and leave it locked
context: Luggage service staff check that an adjustable pull handle reaches its working setting and retains that setting before returning the case to use. A handle left between its locking holes can collapse during pulling. This bench task uses a compact case held in a service cradle and a native spring pin locking mechanism.
scoring: Score zero until the spring pin has withdrawn beyond 45 mm. Moving the handle beyond 5 mm before that happens invalidates the episode permanently. While handle extension is strictly between 5 mm and 75 mm the pin must remain beyond 45 mm or the episode scores zero permanently. Otherwise an episode that has unlocked earns 0.25. Extension strictly within 2 mm of 80 mm earns 0.5. If the pin also returns below 2 mm and handle speed is below 4 mm per second then score 0.75. Both grippers must open beyond 35 mm and robot contact with the handle and pin must be absent within 1 mm for full conditions. Those conditions earn 0.9 until they hold continuously for two seconds and then earn 1.0. Interrupting the conditions resets that hold. Positions and release conditions are sampled at 20 Hz. The final score is used.
fidelity: A compact rigid luggage body is fixed in a bench service cradle. Wheels are visual rigid cylinders and do not roll. The pull handle and spring locking pin use native joints and contact geometry. No fabric or telescoping tube deformation is modelled. The case is not a load bearing mobility aid.
instruction: Set the luggage pull handle to the green working length reference. Leave the handle secured and both hands clear.
setup: Use the standard bimanual YAM station with table height 747.5 mm. x points forward and y points left from the arm base midpoint. A compact rigid luggage case prototype is secured in a service cradle. Its grey body is 140 by 200 by 34 mm with centre x 75 mm and y minus 30 mm and 21 mm above the table. Five ribs 120 by 6 by 4 mm lie on its top at y minus 95 mm then minus 65 mm then minus 35 mm then minus 5 mm then 25 mm. Two fixed black wheel proxies have radius 20 mm and thickness 12 mm. Their centres are at x 25 mm and y minus 145 mm and 85 mm and 20 mm above the table. A blue sliding pull handle runs along x with its root at x 140 mm and y minus 30 mm and 60 mm above the table. It starts retracted. A separate green spring locking pin has its fixed guide at x 140 mm and y 25 mm and 60 mm above the table. It starts engaged. The handle has two transverse locking holes 80 mm apart. A green working length reference stands at x 320 mm and y minus 105 mm. Its size is 3 by 35 by 70 mm with centre 35 mm above the table. The original white length mark remains at x 320 mm and y minus 75 mm. The case and handle are rigid polymer prototypes with a metal pin and spring. The case is fixed for service and the wheels do not roll. Exact collision solids and masses are in scene_inventory.json.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds.
reset_notes: Restore every object to the starting pose in scene_inventory.json and every joint to zero. Nothing is consumed. Use one epoch with seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
scores: Dream 1 run: 0.0 in 2400 steps. Scripted demo: 1.0 in 352 steps.
